memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Put the altar in front of the curtain that shields the ark of the covenant law — before the atonement cover that is over the tablets of the covenant law — where I will meet with you." - Exodus 30:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God specifies exactly where the incense altar stands: right in front of the curtain, as close to His presence as anything could be without passing through. The place of prayer was positioned at the very threshold of the Most Holy Place, directly before the mercy seat.

Think about what that location means. Prayer was set up as near to God as the design allowed. It stood before the atonement cover — the place where mercy covered the law. Prayer's proper address has always been the mercy seat, not the judgment seat.

And now the curtain has been torn. Hebrews urges us to approach God's throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need (Heb 4:16). Notice what kind of throne it is called: a throne of grace. When you pray, you are not approaching a bench where your record is being examined. You are coming to the place where mercy sits. Come as near as the design allows — and through Christ, that is all the way in.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I approach God in prayer expecting judgment or expecting grace?
What keeps me from drawing as near to God as Christ has made possible?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, prayer belongs at the mercy seat, not the judgment seat. Thank You that through Christ I may come all the way in. Draw me near with confidence today. Amen.
